before.title: 12V Battery Discharge and No-Start from Telematics/DCM Staying Awake
before.description: Multiple 2023-2025 RX owners have reported dead 12V batteries, repeated jump-starts, and intermittent no-start conditions after the vehicle sits overnight or for a few days. The issue has been tied in owner reports and Toyota/Lexus service communications to excessive parasitic draw, often involving the Data Communication Module (DCM)/telematics system or related control modules not entering sleep mode properly. Owners commonly describe the problem appearing on relatively new vehicles with otherwise healthy batteries.
before.solution: Diagnosis should start with a battery state-of-health test and a parasitic draw test after all modules are expected to sleep. Dealers typically check for applicable software updates or service bulletins addressing DCM/module sleep behavior, then recharge or replace the battery if it has been damaged by repeated deep discharge. If draw remains high, isolate the offending circuit and verify telematics, gateway, and body ECU software calibration levels.
symptoms: warning messages after low voltage event
battery replacement does not permanently solve issue

communityRecommendations.content: Ask the dealer to document parasitic draw in milliamps after sleep timeout and verify all telematics/DCM software updates are installed before authorizing another battery replacement.
If the vehicle must sit for long periods, owners often use a smart maintainer to prevent deep discharge while the root cause is being diagnosed.

proposal.title: 12V Battery Discharge and No-Start from Telematics/DCM Staying Awake
proposal.description: Lexus bulletin L-SB-0017-25 applies to 2023-2024 RX350 vehicles and documents a startup Shift System Malfunction message together with battery voltage below 10V near freezing; its remedy is revised ECM logic. The complete RX communication inventory does not tie that condition to a DCM that stays awake, does not extend the bulletin to the 2025 RX, and does not establish the title's overnight parasitic-discharge mechanism or multiple-owner prevalence.
proposal.solution: Test battery state of health and charging output, identify the exact warning and stored codes, and measure key-off current only after the vehicle reaches its specified sleep state. Apply L-SB-0017-25 only when its model-year, symptom and calibration requirements match; otherwise isolate any verified draw before replacing a module or battery. This is VIN- and diagnosis-specific electrical work; no universal battery, DCM or retail part is asserted.

before.title: AC Evaporator Core Refrigerant Leak
before.description: The AC evaporator core in the RX develops pinhole leaks from internal corrosion, causing slow refrigerant loss. The system gradually loses cooling capacity over weeks or months as the charge leaks through the evaporator. This is an expensive repair because the entire dashboard must be removed to access the evaporator.
before.solution: Replace the AC evaporator core and receiver/drier. This requires full dashboard removal, which is 8-12 hours of labor. Recharge the system with the correct amount of R-134a refrigerant. Replacing the expansion valve at the same time is recommended while the dash is apart.
symptoms: AC gradually stops blowing cold air
AC works after recharge but loses cooling within weeks
Humidity or fog on windshield when using AC
Visible refrigerant dye leak at evaporator drain

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — RX350 AC evaporator replacement procedure and cost discussion

communityRecommendations.content: Before paying for evaporator replacement, have a UV dye test done to confirm the evaporator is the source. The condenser and compressor seals are much cheaper to replace and should be ruled out first.

proposal.solution: Have a qualified A/C technician recover and measure the refrigerant and locate the leak with the model-appropriate procedure before opening the HVAC case. before.title: Brake Pedal Vibration/Grinding and Extended Stopping Feel from ABS Actuator Software Logic
before.description: Some current-generation RX owners report an unexpectedly harsh ABS event at low speeds over bumps, manhole covers, or rough pavement, accompanied by grinding or pedal kickback and a sensation of reduced braking for a moment. This complaint pattern has appeared on Toyota/Lexus TNGA-K vehicles and is documented in owner discussions and complaints, where drivers describe the vehicle seeming to surge forward briefly while the ABS modulates. While often intermittent, it can be alarming in urban stop-and-go driving.
before.solution: Road-test the vehicle on the same surface conditions to reproduce the concern and scan the brake/ABS system for stored codes. Dealers should check for calibration updates to the skid control ECU/ABS software and inspect wheel-speed sensor tone rings, tire size uniformity, and suspension components that could trigger false wheel-slip detection. If no hardware fault is found, software reprogramming is the most common corrective path.

communityRecommendations.content: When visiting the dealer, note the exact speed, road surface, and whether the steering wheel was turned; reproducible conditions help separate normal ABS behavior from a calibration issue.
Verify all four tires match in size, wear, and pressure, since wheel-speed differences can aggravate false ABS intervention.

proposal.title: Brake Pedal Vibration/Grinding and Extended Stopping Feel from ABS Actuator Software Logic
proposal.description: Direct current-generation RX 350h reports describe individual crunchy, buzzing or vibrating brake-pedal sensations, including conditions while stationary and at road speed. They do not establish the frozen rough-road low-speed ABS event, a momentary reduction in braking, or skid-control software logic as the cause. No exact 2023-2025 Lexus RX communication in the complete inventory supports that mechanism or a routine software remedy.
proposal.solution: Treat any change in braking response as safety-relevant: record the speed and road condition, scan the brake and stability systems, inspect tires, wheel-speed inputs and hardware, and reproduce the symptom with a qualified technician. Distinguish normal hybrid brake-actuator or regenerative transitions from a fault before applying calibration or replacing parts. This is symptom- and diagnosis-specific brake work; no universal software update, actuator or retail part is asserted.

before.title: Front Camera / Millimeter-Wave Radar Misalignment Causing PCS and Driver-Assist Warnings
before.description: Owners of the current-generation RX have reported recurring messages such as 'Pre-Collision System Malfunction,' 'Front Camera Unavailable,' or temporary loss of adaptive cruise and lane functions. These complaints appear in NHTSA filings and owner forums, often after windshield replacement, minor impacts, heavy rain, or sometimes with no obvious trigger. The issue is commonly related to camera/radar obstruction, calibration drift, connector faults, or software sensitivity in the Lexus Safety System+ suite.
before.solution: Inspect the windshield camera area and front radar emblem area for dirt, condensation, damage, or non-OEM replacement parts. Perform a scan for ADAS-related DTCs, then complete static/dynamic calibration of the forward recognition camera and millimeter-wave radar if alignment is out of spec. If warnings persist, dealers may apply software updates or replace a faulty sensor/module after confirming power, ground, and network integrity.

communityRecommendations.content: After any windshield replacement, confirm the shop can perform Lexus-compatible ADAS calibration; many intermittent warnings start after glass work.
Keep the radar emblem and upper windshield camera area clean and avoid stickers, dashcams, or tint strips that can interfere with the sensors.

Perform calibration only when the exact repair procedure requires it after glass, alignment or component work, and replace a sensor or module only after power, network, damage and calibration checks identify it. before.title: Infotainment Screen Freezing, Wireless CarPlay/Android Auto Dropouts, and Rebooting Head Unit
before.description: The new-generation RX uses Lexus Interface, and owners have widely reported frozen center displays, laggy touch response, black screens, audio loss, and unstable wireless smartphone integration. Complaints and forum threads describe random head-unit reboots, failure to reconnect to Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, and navigation/audio functions becoming unavailable until the vehicle is restarted. The pattern suggests a mix of software bugs, phone compatibility issues, and occasional hardware faults.
before.solution: First verify the head unit has the latest Lexus Interface software and update the connected phone OS. Delete and re-pair the phone, test both wireless and wired connections, and check for TSBs or dealer software campaigns addressing multimedia instability. If the unit continues freezing or rebooting, dealers may replace the display/audio ECU or related USB hub after documenting the failure.

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often report better stability after removing old phone pairings, rebooting the phone, and re-pairing only one primary device.
If wireless CarPlay remains unreliable, use a high-quality USB-C cable temporarily to determine whether the issue is wireless-stack related.

proposal.title: Infotainment Screen Freezing, Wireless CarPlay/Android Auto Dropouts, and Rebooting Head Unit
proposal.description: Lexus tech tip L-TT-0340-25 applies to 2023-2025 RX350, RX350h and RX500h vehicles and to 2024-2025 RX450h+ vehicles. It instructs technicians to preserve and retrieve Multimedia Recorder data for CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, rebooting, screen and connectivity concerns, while stating that MMR is a quality-investigation tool rather than a case-by-case diagnostic tool. Direct owner discussion supports individual integration problems, but neither source establishes wide prevalence or one shared software, phone, USB or hardware cause.
proposal.solution: Record the date, time, phone, connection type and exact symptom. If dealer assistance is needed, avoid restarting the head unit solely as a workaround before the event is captured because L-TT-0340-25 says a restart can erase MMR data; a qualified technician can retrieve logs when requested and then follow the exact diagnostic path. Verify phone, pairing and available software without assuming one cause, and replace hardware only after diagnosis. This is event- and equipment-specific multimedia diagnosis; no universal phone, cable, USB hub, display or head unit is asserted.

before.title: Excessive Oil Consumption 2GR Engine
before.description: The 3.5L 2GR-FE V6 in the RX350 consumes excessive oil, often requiring a quart every 1,500-3,000 miles. The piston ring design allows oil to bypass into the combustion chamber, and the PCV system contributes to the problem. Toyota acknowledged the issue with a TSB covering piston ring replacement.
before.solution: Dealer oil consumption test to document the rate. If excessive, piston ring replacement is the definitive fix under Toyota TSB. Check and clean the PCV valve as a first step. Monitor oil level weekly and keep a log of consumption for warranty claims.
symptoms: Oil level drops 1+ quart between changes
Fouled spark plugs from oil burning

communityRecommendations.content: Switching from 0W-20 to 5W-30 synthetic (Toyota also approves this weight) has reduced oil consumption by 30-50% for many RX350 owners without voiding warranty.

proposal.title: Excessive Oil Consumption 2GR Engine
proposal.description: The frozen citation is materially mismatched. The complete exact RX communication inventory does not substantiate a piston-ring defect, a quart-per-1,500-to-3,000-mile rate, PCV causation or a Lexus piston-replacement program across the frozen 2007-2017 range.
proposal.solution: Verify the oil level and specification, document additions and distance, and inspect for external leaks before performing an engine-specific consumption test. Check the PCV system, compression and other causes only as indicated by diagnosis; do not apply the 2AZ-FE bulletin or prescribe piston rings to a 2GR RX. This is engine- and diagnosis-specific work; no universal PCV valve, piston set, oil viscosity or retail part is asserted.

before.title: Power Steering Pressure Hose Leak and Pump Whine from Fluid Loss
before.description: Both RX300 and RX330 generations commonly develop power steering fluid leaks, especially from the high-pressure hose and related line connections. Owners report red fluid on the driveway, groaning or whining while turning, and heavier steering effort as fluid level drops. If ignored, the pump can run dry and fail, increasing repair cost significantly.
before.solution: Inspect the pressure hose, return lines, reservoir, and pump area for wetness, then confirm whether the leak is from the crimped hose section or a fitting. Replace the leaking hose or line assembly, refill with the correct fluid, and bleed the system fully; if the pump has been noisy for long, inspect for internal damage. Cleaning the subframe and alternator area is important because leaked fluid can spread widely.
symptoms: Fluid on driveway or under engine cradle

communityRecommendations.content: Owners recommend replacing aging return hoses at the same time as the pressure hose if they are soft or sweating, since labor overlap is significant.
After repair, bleed the steering system with the front wheels raised to reduce pump cavitation noise.

proposal.title: Power Steering Pressure Hose Leak and Pump Whine from Fluid Loss
proposal.description: Direct reports document individual pressure-, return-line and other steering-fluid leaks on RX300 and RX330 vehicles, so the symptom is real. They also show that fluid can spread and that the source must be isolated. Lexus L-SB-0016-14 covers a different, tightly bounded right-side OEM steering-rack leak on North American-built 2004-2009 RX330/RX350 vehicles; it does not prove a universal high-pressure-hose failure across the frozen 2000-2006 page.
proposal.solution: Confirm that the fluid and reservoir loss are from the steering system, clean the area, and trace the active leak across the pump, pressure hose, return line, fittings and rack. Replace only the confirmed leaking assembly, use the exact vehicle fluid and bleeding procedure, and inspect a pump that has run low. This is source- and fitment-specific hydraulic steering repair; no universal hose, pump, rack kit or retail part is asserted.

before.title: Rear Main Seal / Engine Oil Leak at Timing Cover and Lower Engine Seals
before.description: RX330 owners frequently report persistent engine oil leaks that are often diagnosed at the rear main seal, timing cover area, or other lower engine sealing surfaces. The leak may start as minor seepage but can progress to oil spots on the driveway, burning oil odor, and contamination of the lower engine and subframe. Because access is labor-intensive, especially if the rear main seal is involved, repair costs can become substantial even when the leak itself is not immediately catastrophic.
before.solution: Clean the engine thoroughly and use dye or UV tracing to identify the true source, since valve cover, timing cover, and rear main leaks can be misidentified. Repair involves replacing the failed seal or resealing the timing cover, often while addressing nearby components with overlapping labor. If the leak is minor, some owners monitor oil level until the leak worsens enough to justify the labor.
symptoms: Oil residue on lower engine or transmission bellhousing
Smoke from oil contacting hot exhaust components

communityRecommendations.content: Use UV dye before authorizing a rear main seal job; several owners found the actual leak was higher up at the valve cover or timing cover.
If transmission removal is required, owners often replace related wear items with overlapping labor to save money later.

proposal.title: Rear Main Seal / Engine Oil Leak at Timing Cover and Lower Engine Seals
proposal.description: Direct RX330 discussion documents apparent lower-engine oil leaks and demonstrates the diagnostic risk: one owner suspected a rear main seal, found the inspection area dry and traced the oil to valve-cover leakage. The complete exact RX communication inventory does not establish a recurring 2004-2006 rear-main, timing-cover and lower-seal defect as one identity, nor does it prove prevalence or a shared repair.
proposal.solution: Clean the engine, verify the fluid and monitor the highest wet point; use dye or the model-appropriate inspection procedure when needed. Inspect valve covers and other sources before condemning the rear main seal or timing cover, because transmission removal or major resealing should follow proof of the source. This is leak-location-specific engine repair; no universal seal kit, reseal package or retail part is asserted.

before.title: Steering Intermediate Shaft Clunk and Loose Steering Feel Over Bumps
before.description: Second-generation RX330 models commonly develop a clunk or knock felt through the steering column, especially at low speed over small bumps or during quick steering inputs. Lexus issued service information for intermediate steering shaft noise, and owners often describe the sensation as a loose front end despite no obvious play in major suspension joints. The condition is usually caused by wear or lash in the intermediate shaft splines or joints rather than a catastrophic steering rack failure.
before.solution: Road test over small road imperfections to reproduce the column knock, then isolate the sound from the shaft, rack mounts, and front suspension links. Replacement of the intermediate steering shaft is the usual fix; some vehicles also need inspection of rack bushings and front stabilizer links if multiple noises are present. An alignment is not always required but front-end inspection should accompany the repair.
symptoms: Noise during quick left-right steering input
Front-end rattle with no obvious suspension failure

communityRecommendations.content: Owners recommend confirming the noise source before replacing struts or sway bar links, because the steering shaft clunk can mimic suspension noise.
Use the updated Lexus/Toyota shaft part rather than a salvage-yard original to reduce the chance of repeat noise.

proposal.title: Steering Intermediate Shaft Clunk and Loose Steering Feel Over Bumps
proposal.description: Direct RX reports document steering-wheel popping or clunking, but the discussions only suggest an intermediate shaft among several possible sources and do not prove it caused the reported noise. proposal.solution: Reproduce the noise safely and inspect the steering column and intermediate joints together with rack mounts, tie rods, strut mounts and stabilizer links. Replace or service an intermediate shaft only after the noise or play is localized there under the exact repair procedure, then verify steering operation and alignment requirements. This is source- and fitment-specific steering diagnosis; no universal shaft or retail part is asserted.

before.title: 8-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder
before.description: The Aisin 8-speed automatic in the fourth-generation RX develops a noticeable shudder or vibration during light throttle acceleration, particularly in the 25-45 MPH range during torque converter lockup. The shudder is caused by torque converter clutch material wearing into the transmission fluid, degrading its friction properties.
before.solution: Perform a transmission fluid drain-and-fill with Toyota WS ATF, which resolves the shudder in most cases. Severe cases may require a torque converter replacement. Do not flush — only drain and refill. Plan to change the fluid every 30,000-40,000 miles despite the "lifetime" fluid claim.
symptoms: Feeling like driving over rumble strips

before.title: U140E/U151E Automatic Transmission Failure from Burned Planetary Gearset and Delayed Engagement
before.description: Early first-generation RX300 models are well known for premature automatic transmission failure, especially on AWD vehicles but also on FWD examples. Owners report delayed engagement into Drive or Reverse, harsh shifting, slipping on acceleration, and eventual loss of movement; teardown reports commonly cite burned clutches and damaged planetary gear components. The issue is widely documented in owner communities, repair databases, and NHTSA complaints, and is often attributed to a transmission that runs hot and is heavily stressed by vehicle weight.
before.solution: Diagnosis usually starts with checking fluid condition, line pressure behavior, and whether engagement delay or flare shifts are present when warm. In most cases, fluid changes do not cure an already failing unit; the durable fix is a quality rebuild or replacement transmission, often with updated hard parts and careful inspection of the cooler and valve body. Many owners also add an auxiliary transmission cooler after replacement to reduce repeat failures.
symptoms: Delayed engagement into Drive or Reverse
Engine revs increase with little vehicle movement

This is transmission-code- and diagnosis-specific repair; no universal rebuild kit, cooler or retail part is asserted.

before.title: Water Pump Premature Failure
before.description: The water pump on the RX fails prematurely due to internal seal and bearing wear. Coolant weeps from the pump weep hole and the bearing develops play, causing a whining or grinding noise from the front of the engine. Failure rates are highest between 60,000-100,000 miles.
before.solution: Replace the water pump and thermostat assembly. Use OEM Aisin or Denso parts for reliability. Replace the drive belt and tensioner at the same time. Flush the cooling system with new Toyota Super Long Life Coolant during the repair.

Whining noise from front of engine
